Agile project management relies on two related concepts that shape how teams develop and deliver work: iteration and incremental delivery. Iterative Iterative work means revisiting something that has already been created and improving it based on what the team learns. For example, a team might release an early version of a customer portal, review user feedback, and revise its navigation in a later iteration. Iteration is important when the team cannot determine the best solution from planning alone. Each review provides evidence that can influence later decisions. Incremental Incremental work means delivering the project in usable portions instead of completing the entire solution before anything is released or reviewed. A team building the same customer portal might deliver account registration first, followed later by billing features and reporting. Agile project management

Why do we need Agile Project Management? We need Agile Project Management because traditional project management methodologies often struggle to adapt to the rapidly changing demands of modern business environments. Agile offers several benefits: Flexibility: Teams can quickly respond to changing requirements and priorities, delivering value effectively in dynamic environments. Customer Satisfaction: Frequent collaboration and short development cycles ensure products meet customer needs and expectations. Efficiency: Iterative development and continuous improvement streamline processes, reduce waste, and accelerate time-to-market. Transparency: Open communication within teams and with stakeholders builds trust and accountability. Adaptability: Teams learn from experience and adjust their approach, improving outcomes and reducing the risk of project failure.
